description: A single-panel Temperature–Time schematic showing the thermomechanical processing routes of Fe–Mn–Al–C low-density steel. The vertical axis is labelled "Temperature" and the horizontal axis "Time"; neither axis carries numeric ticks, so only relative positions are shown. The schedule starts with a high plateau labelled "1100-1200 °C" under the word "Solution", then descends along a zig-zag segment labelled "Hot rolling" to a lower plateau. A second zig-zag at the bottom is labelled "Cold rolling". The path then rises to an annealing plateau labelled "1100-1200 °C" (annotated "Annealing") with a lower interval labelled "600-800 °C", and ends in an aging stage labelled "450-700 °C" drawn as a dashed line and annotated "Aging". Four coloured arrows branch the routes: Route 1 (green), Route 2 (red), Route 3 (blue) and Route 4 (purple, dashed). The figure demonstrates the overall sequence solution treatment → hot rolling → cold rolling → annealing → aging, and shows that alternative combinations of these steps define four distinct processing routes for this steel family.

subfigures.description: One Temperature (y, °C; no scale) versus Time (x, no scale) schematic of a processing route. A solution-treatment plateau is labelled 1100-1200 °C; a zig-zag 'Hot rolling' segment follows; a lower zig-zag is labelled 'Cold rolling'; an annealing plateau is labelled 1100-1200 °C with a lower interval 600-800 °C; an aging stage is labelled 450-700 °C (dashed line). Four coloured arrows mark Route 1 (green), Route 2 (red), Route 3 (blue) and Route 4 (purple dashed).

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic with 'Temperature' on the vertical axis and 'Time' on the horizontal axis; neither axis has numeric tick values or units printed.
The solution-treatment stage is labelled 'Solution' at a temperature of '1100-1200 °C'.
Hot rolling is drawn as a zig-zag (rolling pass) on a descending temperature segment between the solution plateau and a lower plateau.
Cold rolling is drawn as a second zig-zag at low temperature at the bottom of the schedule.
The annealing plateau is labelled '1100-1200 °C' with 'Annealing', and a lower temperature interval is labelled '600-800 °C'.
The aging stage is labelled '450-700 °C' and drawn with a dashed line, annotated 'Aging'.
Four coloured arrows designate the routes: Route 1 green, Route 2 red, Route 3 blue, Route 4 purple dashed.
The caption describes the figure as abstract images of hot and cold rolling, annealing and aging processes of Fe-Mn-Al-C steel.
The citing text states the forging ingot is homogenized at 1100-1250 °C for 1-3 h and then hot-rolled to 2-5 mm thickness between 1100 and 850 °C.
The citing text states that for austenite-base Fe-Mn-C-Al steels the hot-rolled steel can be rapidly cooled to room temperature then isothermally annealed and aged (Route 1 in Fig. 3).
The citing text states that cold rolling and recrystallization annealing are used to tailor the delta-ferrite size, texture and kappa-carbide (Route 2 in Fig. 3).

The citing text states that aging at 500-700 °C for 0.5-2 h (Routes 3 and 4 in Fig. 3) is beneficial to the nucleation of nano precipitates; note this 500-700 °C range differs from the '450-700 °C' printed on the aging stage of the figure.
